a1.say: Let's solve Merge Overlapping Intervals, using the Sort plus Sweep approach.

a1.cap: Merge all overlapping intervals [start, end] and return the result sorted by start. Intervals that touch (one ends where the next starts) also merge.
a1.say: Merge all overlapping intervals start, end and return the result sorted by start. Intervals that touch (one ends where the next starts) also merge.

lines: Merge all overlapping intervals [start, end] and return the result sorted by start. Intervals that touch (one ends where the next starts) also merge.

a1.say: For example, with intervals equals 1, 3, 2, 6, 8, 10, 15, 18, the answer is 1, 6, 8, 10, 15, 18.

a1.cap: Sort by start time. Walk through: if an interval starts before (or exactly when) the last merged interval ends, extend that one; otherwise start a new merged interval.
Let's walk through it with intervals = [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]].
a1.say: Let's walk through it with intervals equals 1, 3, 2, 6, 8, 10, 15, 18.

a1.cap: [2, 6] overlaps, so the last merged interval grows to [1, 6].
a1.say: 2, 6 overlaps, so the last merged interval grows to 1, 6.

a1.cap: Time complexity is O(n log n) and extra space is O(n).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n log n and extra space is O of n.

a1.cap: That's the Sort + Sweep approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
